reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: A group of autosomal recessive dysplasias in which shortening predominantly affects the middle (mesomelic) and distal (acromelic) segments of the limbs, sparing the proximal segment
The Maroteaux type is caused by biallelic variants in NPR2, encoding the natriuretic peptide receptor B that mediates CNP signalling in the growth plate
Presents with disproportionate short stature evident in early childhood, with strikingly short forearms, lower legs, hands and feet
Hands are short and broad with stubby fingers, and there may be limited elbow extension and progressive deformity
The trunk and craniofacial features are relatively preserved, but a short stature with normal intelligence is typical
Radiographs show shortened, sometimes bowed radius and ulna, shortened tibia/fibula and short broad metacarpals and phalanges with cone-shaped epiphyses
Heterozygous NPR2 carriers may have isolated short stature, illustrating a dose-dependent effect on linear growth
reference.pathophysiology: Acromesomelic dysplasia, Maroteaux type, is caused by loss-of-function variants in NPR2, encoding natriuretic peptide receptor B, the receptor for C-type natriuretic peptide (CNP). CNP-NPR2 signalling stimulates chondrocyte proliferation and matrix production in the growth plate and is a key positive regulator of endochondral bone growth, acting in part by antagonising the FGFR3 pathway. Deficient receptor function reduces growth-plate activity most markedly in the mesomelic and acromelic limb segments, producing their disproportionate shortening. Other genetic forms involve related BMP/GDF signalling components.
additionalDifferentials: Other mesomelic dysplasias (e.g. Langer, Leri-Weill dyschondrosteosis)
additionalInvestigations: Skeletal survey documenting the acromesomelic pattern of limb shortening and cone-shaped epiphyses
Molecular genetic testing (NPR2 and related genes such as BMPR1B, GDF5)
Growth assessment with segmental body proportion measurements
Radiographs of hands and forearms for metacarpal/phalangeal shortening and forearm bowing
Assessment of parents/siblings given autosomal recessive inheritance and carrier effects on height
redFlags: Progressive forearm or limb deformity limiting function and warranting orthopaedic correction
Neurological symptoms suggesting spinal canal narrowing in the differential dysplasias
Features pointing to an alternative dysplasia with systemic complications
Disproportionate short stature causing significant functional or psychosocial impact
reference.prognosis: Intelligence and lifespan are normal; the main issues are disproportionate short stature and limb deformity, which may require orthopaedic correction, with the overall outlook generally favourable.
pitfalls: Mislabelling the limb-shortening pattern as achondroplasia rather than recognising the acromesomelic distribution
Assuming dominant inheritance when the Maroteaux type is autosomal recessive
Overlooking that heterozygous carriers may have mild isolated short stature
Failing to distinguish it from acrodysostosis and pseudohypoparathyroidism, which have distinct biochemistry
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
GeneReviews / Orphanet: Acromesomelic Dysplasia, Maroteaux Type
management: No disease-specific pharmacotherapy exists, as the defect lies in the CNP receptor itself; care is supportive and orthopaedic
Orthopaedic correction of forearm bowing, radioulnar deformity and limited elbow extension, with consideration of limb-lengthening or osteotomy where function or deformity warrants
Physiotherapy and occupational therapy to preserve joint range of motion and maximise function, with aids adapted to short stature
Serial monitoring of growth and segmental body proportions plotted on appropriate charts
Periodic radiographic surveillance for progressive limb deformity and joint complications
Coordination through a multidisciplinary skeletal dysplasia team including clinical genetics, orthopaedics and physiotherapy
Genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance, with carrier testing and family screening
